text:
pagerduty-bot: INCIDENT ALERT — log-processing-exporter error rate spike detected (rule: log_processor_error_rate > 5% over 2m). paging eng-sre on-call. incident id: INC-2027-03-12-47 :rotating_light:
opsbot: Linking logs: https://logs.redwood.internal/q=service:log-processor+level:error+status:5xx
sam: seeing lots of repeated `Failed to write to sink` errors from node-3 and node-4. Possibly backpressure from S3 emitter.
anya: oncall is @devon, devon are you able to take?
devon: taking. quick check — tailing node-3 logs now. stack traces look like intermittent 503s from the object store, but error messages are noisy and contain session ids.
jordan: confirmed customer-facing feature (async export) will see partial failures; routing to Dedicated jobs might be impacted. tagging pg affected: export-async.
devon: immediate mitigation plan: 1) scale down export concurrency on log-processor to reduce retries 2) add a temporary suppression rule for the noisy error signature so paging quiets while we stabilize 3) open a follow-up to tune the alert expression so it doesn't fire on transient emitter 503s.
lee: how many pagers so far? I configured a burst suppression but it's still spamming team.
opsbot: Active pager count: 6 incidents this hour, 3 distinct rules firing. Auto-suppression window applied: 5m.
sam: devon — for scaling: bump `EXPORT_CONCURRENCY` from 12 -> 6 on node pool `log-prod`? that should reduce requests to S3 and lower retries.
devon: applying change now (kubectl patch) — posting command: ```kubectl -n production set env deployment/log-processor EXPORT_CONCURRENCY=6```
opsbot: Patch applied to deployment/log-processor (revision v2.3.14 -> v2.3.15-canary). Rolling restart initiated.
anya: can someone add a short-lived log-based suppression rule in alerting to avoid duplicate pagers? e.g., exclude known benign message that floods: `"Failed to write to sink: .*connection reset by peer"`
jordan: proposed suppression code (logql): ```err_count = sum(rate({service="log-processor",level="error"} |~ "Failed to write to sink: .*connection reset by peer" [2m])) by (job)
err_total = sum(rate({service="log-processor",level="error"}[2m])) by (job)
fraction = err_count / err_total
fraction > 0.5``` — only fire if more than 50% of errors are not the known benign signature.
sam: we should also add a negative-match at query time to stop alerting on that signature entirely while we stabilize: `|!~ "connection reset by peer"`
devon: adding temporary alert tweak in Grafana Alerting now. I'll create a new rule `log_processor_error_rate_v2_temp` that excludes the connection-reset messages and keeps the threshold a bit higher during the window.
opsbot: New alert rule `log_processor_error_rate_v2_temp` created in folder `eng-sre/in-flight`. Expression includes: `|!~ "connection reset by peer"` and `for: 3m`.
lee: please note we want to avoid losing signal for real 5xxs — ensure we don't suppress `status: 500|502|503` completely.
devon: confirmed. rule excludes messages by regex but still counts status codes.
jordan: dashboard request: can someone add a panel showing `error signature distribution` (top 10 error messages) and `per-node error fraction` so we can spot noisy signatures in the future?
anya: I'll spin up a temp dashboard in `eng-sre > incidents > live-mit` with panels: - error signature heatmap - per-node 5xx rate - export queue depth.
sam: FYI customer impact: we saw ~12% of async exports fail for 7 minutes. OKR: no customer data lost (retries will re-enqueue), but user-facing UIs may have shown failed status briefly. Lets include that in the incident notes.
devon: rolling restarts succeeded on all pods. error rate down to baseline over 8 minutes.
opsbot: Incident INC-2027-03-12-47 state: mitigated -> monitoring. escalation auto-unmute scheduled in 30m.
lee: post-mortem action items I'd like: 1) permanent alert rule rewrite to be signature-aware (whitelist/blacklist), 2) add regex-based noise suppression library to alerting configs, 3) create an export-backpressure dashboard and set sensible defaults for `EXPORT_CONCURRENCY`.
jordan: I'll own the backlog ticket to implement signature-aware rules and a small DSL for `alert_signatures`. Assigning to product: @sam for priority.
anya: creating follow-up tickets: - TICKET-4921 alert: implement signature-aware alerts (owner: jordan) - TICKET-4922 dashboard: export-backpressure + signature panels (owner: anya) - TICKET-4923 infra: set safer default/export concurrency (owner: lee)
sam: thanks everyone. two quick notes for tuning alerts post-incident: 1) lower sensitivity for alerts that are >90% one signature 2) add a `noisy_signatures` regex list with TTL so we can silence for short windows without editing production queries.
devon: one more config snippet I'm adding to the alert rule library (example): ```# alert-signature blacklist example
alert_signatures:
  - name: connection-reset-by-peer
    regex: "Failed to write to sink: .*connection reset by peer"
    ttl: 10m
    action: suppress```
opsbot: Suppression entry `connection-reset-by-peer` added (ttl: 10m) to alert-signatures store.
anya: post-incident followup: I'll schedule a 30-min retro tomorrow to decide whether to keep a permanent signature or improve infra to avoid emitter 503s.
sam: recording customer impact summary in INC-2027-03-12-47: transient export failures impacted ~3% of active users; no data loss; mitigation: reduced concurrency and short suppression; long-term: signature-aware rules + infra retry/backpressure tuning.
devon: closing the live thread but keeping monitoring active until fully green. thanks all. :pray:
